ip_top_stories.title: Thousands of authors seek share of Anthropic copyright settlement
ip_top_stories.summary: A large number of authors are seeking to claim a portion of a copyright settlement reached with Anthropic. The case is significant for the ongoing debate over whether AI companies' use of copyrighted text for training constitutes infringement and how damages should be distributed among rights holders.

ip_top_stories.title: EU copyright law roundup – first trimester of 2026
ip_top_stories.summary: A comprehensive review of EU copyright law developments in the first quarter of 2026, covering legislative and judicial activity relevant to AI and intellectual property. The roundup addresses ongoing tensions between AI training practices and existing copyright frameworks across EU member states.

ip_top_stories.title: AI Music Generator Can't Duck DMCA Claim
ip_top_stories.summary: A court has ruled that an AI music generator cannot avoid a claim brought under the Digital Millennium Copyright Act. The decision is notable for its implications on AI-generated content and the applicability of existing copyright enforcement mechanisms to AI tools.

ip_top_stories.title: As publishers block the Wayback Machine over AI scraping fears, the preservation of the web's public record is threatened
ip_top_stories.summary: Publishers increasingly blocking the Internet Archive's Wayback Machine in response to fears about AI scraping is putting the long-term preservation of the public web record at risk. The trend highlights tensions between rights holders seeking to control how their content is used for AI training and the broader public interest in digital preservation.

ip_top_stories.title: Is the government's stance on AI copyright holding back the UK tech scene?
ip_top_stories.summary: The article examines whether the UK government's current position on AI and copyright — including proposals around text and data mining exceptions — is hampering the competitiveness of the UK technology sector. It considers arguments from both the creative industries and AI developers about the economic consequences of the policy debate.

ip_further_links.title: AI Startups Have These Copyright Lawyers on Speed Dial
ip_further_links.summary: A look at the specialist copyright lawyers being retained by AI startups to navigate the growing volume of litigation and regulatory scrutiny around training data and IP.

ip_further_links.title: Analysing China's stricter examination standards for AI-related patent applications
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis of China's tightened examination criteria for AI-related patent applications and what this means for IP strategy in the sector.

ip_further_links.title: Monkey selfie from 15 years ago accidentally sets precedent for AI copyright dispute
ip_further_links.summary: The famous monkey selfie case — which established that non-human authors cannot hold copyright — is being cited as an influential precedent in current disputes over ownership of AI-generated content.

ip_further_links.title: AI-generated content should be clearly labelled to help people spot fakes, committee says — The Globe and Mail
ip_further_links.summary: A parliamentary or regulatory committee has recommended that AI-generated content carry clear labels to help the public identify synthetic media, raising implications for publishing and copyright transparency.

ip_further_links.title: Bologna Children's Book Fair 2026: AI Takes Center Stage [Metered]
ip_further_links.summary: AI was a dominant theme at the 2026 Bologna Children's Book Fair, with publishers and illustrators debating the implications of generative AI tools for the children's book industry and the rights of human creators.

ip_further_links.title: Generative AI – IP cases and policy tracker — Mishcon de Reya LLP
ip_further_links.summary: Law firm Mishcon de Reya's regularly updated tracker compiles ongoing generative AI intellectual property cases and policy developments across key jurisdictions.

ip_further_links.title: Australian Creatives Push Back Against 'AI Theft' — The Good Men Project
ip_further_links.summary: Australian creative professionals are organising opposition to the unauthorised use of their work to train AI models, framing the practice as theft and calling for stronger legislative protections.

ip_further_links.title: AI in the patent industry: Don't believe the hype. Believe the data. — IPKat
ip_further_links.summary: IPKat examines data-driven evidence on the actual impact of AI tools on the patent industry, pushing back against inflated claims about AI's transformative effect on patent prosecution and examination.

ip_further_links.title: First Quarter HBG Sales Rose 2% [Metered]
ip_further_links.summary: Hachette Book Group reported a 2% rise in sales for the first quarter, offering a snapshot of the major trade publishing market amid ongoing industry pressures including AI disruption.

ip_further_links.title: Guest Post — Exploring Data Spaces in Scholarly Communications — The Scholarly Kitchen
ip_further_links.summary: A guest post on The Scholarly Kitchen examines the emerging concept of data spaces in scholarly communications and their potential role in managing rights and access to research data in the AI era.
